title: Updraft
tagline: Bounce higher. Never look down.
description: An endless climb up crumbling platforms. Every bounce takes you higher. The only way to lose is to fall.

title: Comet
tagline: Your tail is the weapon.
description: Survive an arena that keeps filling up. You trail fire behind you. Anything that touches it burns away, so every escape route is also a trap.

title: Number Crunch
tagline: Solve fast. Shoot faster.
description: Answers drift down the screen. Shoot the right one. A streak makes them harder, a few misses ease them back.

title: Keystroke
tagline: Type clean, not just quick.
description: A race you win on accuracy, not speed. Every key is tracked. The end screen shows which ones cost you. Needs a physical keyboard.

title: Sinkhole
tagline: Keep falling. Don't get caught.
description: A climbing game upside down. Drop through gaps in the hazards. Something rises underneath, and hesitating is what kills you.

title: Circuit Racer
tagline: Four circuits. Three rivals. One line.
description: Top-down racing on four circuits against a field of three, with a slipstream to work for and split times to chase. Pick your track, your race length and how hard the rivals push. Your fastest lap is the score.

title: Block Buster
tagline: Clear the board and the world changes.
description: A falling-shape puzzle that comes apart properly. Cleared cells drop on their own rather than in rows, so a stack built with holes in it collapses into a chain. Charged cells cut a column out of the pile. Empty the board completely and the blocks, the well and the whole palette restyle into a new world.

title: Neon Drift Delivery
tagline: The clock is the fuel. Pass close.
description: A courier run through city traffic that is trying to drive properly rather than trying to be in your way. Cars follow, indicate, overtake and pull over for you. Every delivery buys time and puts the next drop further out; miss one and the run is over. Boost is only earned by squeezing past.

title: Skyhook
tagline: Speed is the only thing holding you up.
description: Swing between skyscrapers on a grappling hook. The rope is a real pendulum, reeling in at the bottom of an arc speeds you up the way pumping a swing does, and letting go keeps every bit of the speed you had. The gaps get wider the further you go, so swinging safely is a slow way to lose.

title: Tower Stack
tagline: Every miss makes the next one harder.
description: Drop a sliding slab onto the one below it. Whatever hangs over the edge is sheared off, and what is left is all you have to aim at next time. Errors do not cost a life, they cost width. Land one dead centre and you get some of that width back, which is the only thing standing between a good run and arithmetic.

title: Gravity Flip
tagline: One button. Down is negotiable.
description: A precision runner with one control: which way is down. Rooms of spikes, walls and saws are hand-built and dealt out in escalating order, and a flip always costs the same four tiles of ground however fast you are going — so a room that was fair at the start is still fair two hundred rooms later.

title: Ballast
tagline: Stack the hold. Keep her level.
description: Crates drop into a barge that is floating, not fixed. Where you put the weight tilts the hull, and a hull far enough over ships water and ends the voyage. Packing a row tight battens it down and it slides out of the bottom of the hold, so the stack is something you work off rather than something you clear. The crates are odd shapes and awkward sizes, and the heavy ones are heavy.

title: Ember
tagline: One burner. Mind the walls.
description: A patchwork balloon drifting up a gorge at dusk. One control: hold the burner and you rise, let go and you sink. Everything else is reading the gap in the rock ahead and committing early, because a balloon carries its momentum and cannot change its mind. Rock arches, crosswinds, and a gorge that narrows the higher you get.

title: Rift Runner
tagline: Every portal changes the rules.
description: An endless runner with three verbs — jump, slide, and a dash that phases you through solid rift walls. Every so often a portal opens on clear ground, and going through it rewrites the physics: how far you jump, how hard you fall, how fast you run, and in one of them, which way is down. The obstacle patterns are hand-authored phrases rather than random spikes, and every one is provably clearable in every world it can appear in.

title: Endless Mini Golf
tagline: Sink it under par. Bank the difference.
description: Crazy golf that never runs out. Aim, charge and putt through generated holes with walls to bank off, water that costs you a stroke, sand that kills a ball dead and ramps that will not let it stop. You do not get a fixed number of shots — you get a bank. Sink under par and the difference is added to it; go over and it is spent. Run it to zero and the round is over, mid-hole if that is where it happens. Every hole is proved sinkable within par before you ever see it.

title: Winter Base Building
tagline: Wood burns. Wood builds. There is never enough.
description: Endless survival in a winter forest. Three actions a day — gather wood, hunt for meat, or raise the wall — and every night the fire wants feeding and so do you, both of them wanting more as the weeks go on. Wood does two jobs and there is never enough for both, so a camp that funds the fire meets the pack behind a wall that will not hold, and a camp that funds the wall freezes before it gets there. Every seventh night the wolves come and hit whatever you built. Bears are the risk of going out; wolves are the risk of the deadline. Weeks survived is the score.

title: Tank Tactics
tagline: The wall is the second barrel.
description: Arena tanks, and a ricochet you can actually aim. Your shell bounces off the walls, and a shot that has come off a wall hits twice as hard — so banking is worth choosing even when you have a clear line. Dug-in tanks carry plate no straight shot can touch, and the only way through is a bounce, which turns the ricochet from a trick into the thing the game is about. Destructible cover, a shield that takes one hit and recharges, and waves that grow without a ceiling. Waves cleared is the score.

title: Dungeon Dice
tagline: The roll is the question, not the answer.
description: A roguelite where every turn is a roll of five dice, and the game is what you do about it. Swords hit, shields block whatever is winding up, hearts heal, and bolts become charges that keep between turns. Charges buy the three things that make a bad roll answerable: reroll it, bend a face one step around the ring, or bank a die for the turn you will want it. Clear a floor and take an upgrade — a blank face becomes something, or every sword hits harder, or every shield blocks more. Floors survived is the score, and the dungeon grows without a ceiling.

title: Colour Heist
tagline: The doors only open for what you are wearing.
description: Steal gems from a vault of coloured doors. A door only lets you through while you are its colour, and changing colour means standing still for half a second you cannot spare — so the game is routing under a constraint that decides what you can pass through. Gems always sit off the fastest route, which makes taking one a decision rather than a pickup. Every floor is proved crossable by an exact search before it is dealt, and the clock is set from that proof: par plus a margin that shrinks every floor, forever. Gems stolen is the score.

title: Hangman
tagline: Every word can be reasoned out. That is the promise.
description: Hangman with the unfairness taken out of it. Every word in the lexicon is proved solvable from the revealed positions and the ruled-out letters alone — a solver that reasons the way a player does is run over the whole list at every difficulty tier, and the hardest word costs it three wrong guesses of the six you are given. Six wrong a word, three lost rounds a run, and the lexicon gets longer and stranger as you go. A hint costs one of your six, so asking for help brings the gallows a step closer; and from round five the category stops being printed, which gives that one button two uses competing for the same price. Plays properly on a gamepad and a phone rather than falling back to a keyboard.

title: Asteroid Salvage
tagline: Armour is not free. It is heavy.
description: Fly a field, collect salvage, spend it, fly a denser one. The shop offers engine, hull and cargo — and armour is made of something, so every plate you bolt on slows the ship that has to dodge. Acceleration is thrust divided by mass, which makes the three upgrades interfere rather than stack. The next field is announced before the shop closes: a dense field is many rocks slowly and wants a ship that can thread them, a fast one is few rocks quickly and wants a ship that can take the one you did not see. Three fixed purchase orders were run against each other and none of them wins more than half, which is the difference between a shop and a shopping list. Salvage collected is the score.

title: Beat Blocker
tagline: The music is made out of the chart.
description: Three lanes, one shield, and a tempo that will not stop climbing. Attacks fall down the lanes; slide the shield across and block them on the beat, where being on the beat is worth triple. There is no soundtrack to follow because there is no soundtrack: the engine synthesises tones, so the chart is the source of truth and the drums and notes are played from the same list of numbers the game judges you against, which is why the two can never drift apart. The judging windows are in milliseconds rather than fractions of a beat, so a faster phrase asks for more and never for more precision — and the shield takes real time to change lane, so a chart is only dealt if the shield could physically get there. Two hundred phrases were walked looking for one that could not be played. Attacks blocked, weighted by timing, is the score.
